content.document_title: Heart Failure recommendations (2021 vs 2016) - extracted highlights
content.overview: Tabular summary comparing 2021 and 2016 guideline recommendations for diagnosis, device therapy, acute management, and comorbid conditions (AF, CCS, diabetes) in patients with heart failure (HF).

Recommendations for diagnosis of HF.invasive_coronary_angiography: May be considered in patients with HFrEF with intermediate-to-high pre-test probability of coronary artery disease (CAD) and evidence of ischaemia on non-invasive stress testing to establish CAD and its severity.
Recommendations for diagnosis of HF.CT_coronary_angiography: Coronary CT angiography (CTCA) may be considered in patients with low-to-intermediate pre-test probability of CAD or equivocal non-invasive stress tests to rule out coronary artery stenosis.

Recommendations for device therapy in HF.ICD_primary_prevention: An implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) should be considered to reduce risk of sudden death and all-cause mortality in symptomatic HFrEF (NYHA II–III) with LVEF ≤35% despite ≥3 months of optimal medical therapy (OMT), provided life expectancy and functional status justify implantation.
Recommendations for device therapy in HF.CRT: Cardiac resynchronisation therapy (CRT) is recommended for symptomatic patients in sinus rhythm with QRS duration ~130–149 ms with LBBB morphology and LVEF ≤35% despite OMT to improve symptoms and reduce morbidity and mortality; consideration for 'upgrade' to CRT in patients with significant RV pacing or worsening HF despite device therapy.

Recommendations for management of patien.diuretics: Combination of a loop diuretic with a thiazide-type diuretic or a potassium-sparing adjunct may be considered for patients with resistant congestion.
Recommendations for management of patien.vasodilators: Intravenous vasodilators may be considered in hypertensive acute HF to improve symptoms and reduce congestion.
Recommendations for management of patien.opioids: Routine use of opiates is not recommended; may be used cautiously in selected patients for severe dyspnoea/anxiety.
Recommendations for management of patien.short_term_MCS: Short-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS) may be considered in refractory cardiogenic shock depending on patient age, comorbidities and neurological function.

Recommendations for management of patien.anticoagulation: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are recommended in preference to vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) for HF patients with AF who are eligible (non-valvular AF), based on stroke risk assessment (e.g., CHA2DS2-VASc).
Recommendations for management of patien.rate_control: Beta-blockers should be considered for short- and long-term rate control in patients with HF and AF.
Recommendations for management of patien.rhythm_control_and_ablation: Catheter ablation may be considered in selected patients with symptomatic AF, persistent symptoms despite medical therapy, or when rhythm control is preferred; AV node ablation with pacing may be considered in specific cases.

Recommendations for management of patien.revascularisation: Coronary revascularisation may be considered to relieve persistent symptoms of angina in patients with HF and CCS despite optimal anti-anginal/medical therapy.

Recommendations for management of patien.SGLT2_inhibitors_class: SGLT2 inhibitors (examples listed: canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, others) are recommended in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) at risk of cardiovascular events to reduce hospitalisations for HF, major adverse CV events, progression of renal disease, and CV death.
Recommendations for management of patien.empagliflozin_specific: Empagliflozin is noted as a specific agent that may be considered in patients with T2DM to prevent or delay onset of HF and to prolong life.

content.notes: Extraction focused on high-level recommendations visible on the page. Drug classes and device indications summarized; guideline class levels and exact wording abbreviated for brevity.
